C-DOC-CHANGE-JOURNAL.Name: Mini-git document change journal: a UI-free renderer library that records who/what/when for every change to an open document (in-app edits, external writes, system rewrites), computes two-level diffs between any two recorded states on the existing diff-match-patch engine, and exposes a query API — the shared foundation for agent-edit visibility, conflict handling, review and file recovery
C-DOC-CHANGE-JOURNAL.ApprovalBasis: Owner approved 2026-10-23 with the single word "ок" over the draft report, accepting both flagged judgment calls as recommended: (1) the dirty+liveReload silent-overwrite repair ships as its OWN small fix bundle, not inside this change; (2) v1 stays session-scoped with no disk persistence. Origin: the owner's direction ("встроенный мини-гит дифф — универсальный модуль, объект-функция, который покажет кто что когда правил и поможет конфликты правок решать" — a built-in mini-git diff: a universal module showing who changed what and when, and helping resolve edit conflicts) and the owner-side backlog entry "Mini-git document change journal", recorded the same day. Status returned to draft on 2026-10-27 after three rounds of four-corner review; the approval above no longer covers the text. Next step per protocol: correct the findings, pass two consecutive clean four-corner reviews of the corrected spec, obtain fresh owner approval, and only then run grace-plan.
C-DOC-CHANGE-JOURNAL.Summary: Four planned features need the same three answers about an open document — who changed it, what changed, and when — and today Mark has only a fragment of the machinery: a per-tab ring of five pre-reload snapshots (store/diffSnapshots.js) feeding one manual diff view, recorded at four snapshot sites and two opened-baseline sites in the live-reload and open paths. The 2026-10-23 code read also confirmed a live defect in that path: with liveReload ON (the default), an external write silently REPLACES a dirty tab's buffer (APPLY_FILE_CHANGE (editor.js 2416-2573) — the condition `isSaved || liveReload || ...` bypasses the conflict banner whenever liveReload is on); the unsaved text survives only inside the snapshot ring. This change builds the shared foundation as a UI-free renderer library: an append-only per-document journal of ChangeRecords {stateRef, timestamp, actor{kind}, trigger} with triggers for in-app edit pauses, external write batches (consumed from the existing watcher pipeline, not replacing it), and system rewrites; a two-level diff API (coarse block-anchored hunks plus fine line/word detail inside changed blocks) built on the existing diff-match-patch dependency; kind-level attribution (user / external / system) with the actor model reserving label+confidence fields for later identity attribution; and an explicit external-write batch policy (minimum quiet gap plus a forced cut under continuous writes, with atomic rename-writes as the clean single-event case). store/diffSnapshots.js becomes a thin consumer of the journal while keeping its public call shape and ring semantics, so the existing diff view and its tests stay green. The library ships with no UI, no disk writes, and no Rust changes; every consumer surface (agent-edit visibility flash/rail, conflict merge UI, review accept/reject, file history) is a separate change bundle reading this API.

Problem.Description: Mark's agent-era roadmap has four consumers that all need per-document change history: (1) the agent-edits-visible feature (backlog, 2026-10-23) must know which regions an external writer changed and when; (2) the dirty-tab + external-write conflict path must be able to compare base/mine/theirs — and the 2026-10-23 code read proved that path is defective TODAY: with liveReload ON (default, preferences.js:149) an external write overwrites a dirty buffer silently (APPLY_FILE_CHANGE (editor.js 2416-2573; the gate is at 2458/2463 with the conflict branch at 2516): the reload branch runs whenever `isSaved || liveReload || readOnlyReload || tab.watchMode` holds, so liveReload alone forces the swap on an unsaved tab; only the snapshot ring preserves the lost text); (3) the review/tracked-changes item (2026-10-19) needs stable document states to accept/reject against; (4) local file recovery (the 2026-10-18 Obsidian-audit candidate) needs "what did this document look like N minutes ago". Today the only shared asset is store/diffSnapshots.js — a ring of five snapshots recorded opportunistically before live reloads, consumed by one manual diff view, with no attribution, no in-app-edit records, no query API, and no batch boundary definition. Each consumer building its own history would duplicate the same machinery four times with divergent semantics. The owner's direction (2026-10-23) names the shape: a universal object/function module — a mini-git without git — that answers who/what/when once, for everyone.

Goals.R-1: Journal (ledger): an append-only, session-scoped, in-memory journal per open tab (two tabs on one file keep two journals). Each ChangeRecord carries {sequence (monotonic append ordinal — the ordering key), stateRef (full-content state reference), snapshotClass ('ring' | 'opened' | 'event'), pathnameAtWrite (journal metadata, not part of the diffable state), timestamp (informational only), actor{kind, label?, confidence?}, trigger, stats{lines, utf8Bytes}}. Triggers recorded: in-app edit (coalesced on a typing pause; class 'event', never 'ring'), external write batch (class 'event'), system rewrite (class 'event'), pre-reload checkpoint (class 'ring', appended synchronously at the recordSnapshot call site before the reload is applied), and disk-load (class 'opened', written when a file lands in a tab — open, reopen, session restore or a completed external reload). Ordering is append order by sequence; timestamps never decide order. Untitled tabs without a pathname are not journaled (same rule as today's snapshots).
Goals.R-2: Two-level diff API: a pure, deterministic diff(stateA, stateB) returning hunks at two granularities — coarse hunks keyed by content-derived block anchors, plus fine line/word detail inside each changed block — built on the existing diff-match-patch dependency (^1.0.5, package.json:58) with Diff_Timeout pinned to 0 so a result never depends on machine speed; no new diff library is introduced. Anchors come from markdown alone, never from the transient muya ag-N ids, which are minted per parse and are not stored with a state: the block stream is the headless block lexer src/muya/lib/parser/marked/lexer.js with its shipped options pinned (gfm, frontMatter, footnote, superSubScript), and each token type maps to one blockType from a fixed vocabulary (frontmatter, h1..h6, paragraph, list-item, blockquote, code, table, hr, html). Granularity stops at the top-level block: a table is one anchor, a list item is one anchor, a code fence is one anchor. A block anchor has two levels: scope and position. The scope is the heading path from the document root, where each heading contributes its text plus its occurrence index among sibling headings with the same text (so two identical headings produce distinct scopes) and front matter or content before the first heading forms the root scope. Position is resolved by a two-phase alignment: headings first, matched by parent scope and index among sibling headings, with a heading's own text excluded from its identity; then blocks inside a matched pair of scopes content-first — LCS/Myers over normalised block text — with the ordinal used only to break ties between blocks whose normalised text is identical. Precedence is identity over content over ordinal. These consequences are the contract: a renamed heading keeps its scope anchor and reports as a changed heading whose children re-anchor to the new text; a block whose type and matched position are unchanged keeps its anchor, so a same-type insertion elsewhere reports one insertion and no move cascade; a removal reports a deletion; a block matching by content in a different scope reports a move. Identical inputs produce identical output, and the alignment cases are snapshot-tested.
Goals.R-3: Attribution model, kind level only in v1: actor.kind is one of user (change made inside this Mark), external (change arrived from disk), system (Mark-applied whole-document transformation). The record shape reserves optional label and confidence fields, but nothing in this change populates identity: process heuristics (lsof "probable: node/ZCode/claude") and announced channels (mark CLI marker) are deferred, and any UI built on the journal must render kind-level truth only ("external change", never "changed by agent X") — consumer bundles own that wording, this bundle ships no UI.
Goals.R-4: External-write batch policy, defined and implemented once in the journal: a batch closes on a minimum quiet gap after the last watcher event, OR is force-cut after a bounded window of continuous writes (so a writer emitting events every ~150 ms still yields discrete batches), with atomic rename-writes treated as the clean single-event case. The policy consumes the existing Rust watcher events (m013b, 200 ms debounce) and the existing renderer settle (100 ms) plus hash-skip; it does not modify the Rust watcher.
Goals.R-5: Snapshot-ring migration: store/diffSnapshots.js becomes a thin consumer of the journal (the journal is the single recorder of document states). All seven call sites keep their shape: four recordSnapshot calls (BLOCK_SNAPSHOT_BEFORE_RELOAD_DATA editor.js:2474, BLOCK_SNAPSHOT_BEFORE_RELOAD_DISK :2504, the two CONFIRM_* branches :2535 and :2559), two recordOpenedSnapshot calls (RECORD_OPENED_SNAPSHOT_RELOAD editor.js:331/336 for an external reload, RECORD_OPENED_SNAPSHOT_LOAD editor.js:1923/1930 for open, reopen and session restore) and clearSnapshots at editor.js:1416, which must also be called from CLOSE_TABS (editor.js:1540-1572) — the second real close path. recordSnapshot appends synchronously at the call site, never deferred to a batch close, and dedupes only against the newest ring-class record, never against an opened record. The projections keep their exact shipped shapes: latestSnapshot returns {markdown, takenAt} from the newest ring-class record, openedSnapshot returns {markdown, takenAt, kind: 'opened'}, and SNAPSHOT_LIMIT, snapshotCount and __resetDiffSnapshots stay exported with their current semantics. The diff view keeps working unchanged, and the opened-baseline e2e plus every existing diffSnapshots suite stay green.
Goals.R-6: Performance gate: recording a batch is an append with no diff work (the stats it carries are taken from the state being recorded, and the plan measures that cost), and the diff runs only when a consumer asks for it, never inside the watcher, reload or edit path — a source assertion pins that the trigger path calls no diff function; a 10k-line document fixture is pinned in tests with an explicit time budget (number set at plan time from measured baseline), and the reload path's existing behavior (scroll clamp, cursor preservation, 650a555f stale-block drop) is unchanged.
Goals.R-7: The module ships UI-free and renderer-side: no Vue components, no new store actions beyond the library's own API, no new Tauri/Rust commands, no IPC. MODULE_CONTRACT with ROLE appropriate for a library module; consumers render, the journal computes.

Constraints.Item: Nothing is written into .md files, the repository, or any watched/synced folder by this change; the journal is session memory only (cross-session persistence and its storage format are a separate future change with the storage/privacy rules already recorded in the backlog entry).

The existing watcher pipeline is consumed, not replaced: m013b/watch.rs, the renderer watch facade, the 200 ms Rust debounce, the 100 ms settle and the hash-skip stay as they are; the batch policy lives renderer-side in the journal.
diff-match-patch remains the diff engine; no new diff dependency is added.
The existing diff view (components/editorWithTabs/diffView.vue) keeps its behavior and tests; migration must be invisible to it beyond the recording source.

The live-reload behavior chain is untouched by this change: loadChange, scroll clamping (81213fe0), stale-block drop (650a555f) and the dirty-tab paths behave exactly as before — including the live defect described in the Problem; repairing it is explicitly out of scope (see NonGoals) so that the repair is not gated on this module.

Attribution honesty is normative: kind-level truth only; label/confidence fields exist in the model but no code path populates them in this change; consumer bundles own the UI wording rule; this bundle bounds itself to the record shape and the source assertion.
All governed edits ship MODULE_CONTRACT / MODULE_MAP / CHANGE_SUMMARY updates; grace lint --path . --assertions current = 0; graph and verification deltas land in the same bundle as the code.
English repo artifacts; the owner's Russian direction is quoted in translation with the original preserved in the backlog entry.

Memory bound, counted against evictable records only: the journal keeps at most 50 evictable records or 8 MiB of UTF-8 document state per tab, whichever comes first, evicting the oldest non-exempt record first. Exempt are the newest opened-class record and the five newest ring-class records: those six full states are never evicted and are not counted in the 50, so the total ceiling is 50 records plus up to six exempt records, and 8 MiB plus the sum of the exempt states. Older opened-class records are evictable. The journal is cleared when the tab closes, through clearSnapshots called from every close path (FORCE_CLOSE_TAB and CLOSE_TABS), and the plan pins a retained-memory assertion with these numbers.

Journal identity (decided 2026-10-27): the journal is keyed by tab id, not pathname — it is session-scoped and dies with the tab, which is the same identity diffSnapshots already uses, and it survives a rename without a re-key. Every record captures pathnameAtWrite, so a consumer can still name the file and follow a rename in display. No cross-session identity, no pathname-keyed persistence.

Staged delivery inside this bundle (decided 2026-10-27): the plan lands the journal, its three triggers and the batch policy first, then the snapshot-store migration, then the two-level diff last. Splitting the diff layer into a separate C-* bundle was considered and rejected for now — the first consumer, the migrated snapshot store, is in this bundle, while the diff API product consumers are future bundles, so the diff layer ships last inside this bundle. If the plan finds the diff layer needs a separate approval, it stops and asks instead of silently deferring it.
Diagnostics stay content-free: journal logs and error reports carry {tabId, trigger, stats} only — never document text, diff bodies or pathnames; the journal is in-memory and dies with the tab.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Repairing the dirty+liveReload silent overwrite (live defect in APPLY_FILE_CHANGE, editor.js ~2416-2573): recommended as its own small fix bundle so it can ship fast without waiting for this module — routing a dirty tab at external write into the existing conflict banner instead of the silent swap. The owner's decision on bundling (separate fix vs fold into this change) is the flagged open fork; as drafted, this spec does not repair it.
Three-way merge (base/mine/theirs) and any conflict-resolution UI — the follow-up change that both consumes this journal and resolves the conflict path properly.
Identity attribution (lsof process heuristics, mark CLI announcement channel) — deferred with the model fields reserved.
Disk persistence, cross-session retention, and history for closed files or non-open workspace files — v3 territory per the backlog entry.

Any user-facing surface: agent-visibility flash/rail/follow (separate backlog item and future bundle), review accept/reject, history UI, notification cards (the C-NOTIFICATION-SYSTEM source enum already reserves an 'agent' channel; wiring it is that system's future, not this library's).
Tracked-changes review records inside documents (the 2026-10-19 item) — boundary: the journal is local metadata and never enters the file; review records are document content.
Version-control features: branches, commits, user-visible history browsing, .git directories, any git interoperability.
Rust-side journal storage or new backend commands.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Journal unit suite: every trigger (in-app pause, external batch, system rewrite, pre-reload checkpoint, disk-load) produces a ChangeRecord with the right actor.kind and snapshotClass; sequence is monotonic and orders the journal; append-only semantics hold; untitled tabs record nothing; the evictable bound holds (at most 50 evictable records and 8 MiB) while the oldest non-exempt record is evicted first and the six-record exempt set survives.

Two-level diff fixtures (EN+RU markdown: headings, lists, task lists, tables, code fences, footnotes): coarse hunks carry content-derived anchors and never an ag- id; fine detail covers line and word changes; the alignment cases are pinned — a same-type insertion mid-document reports one insertion with no move cascade, a renamed heading keeps its scope and re-anchors its children, two identical headings produce distinct scopes with no cross-talk, a changed table row stays one table anchor, and front matter forms its own scope; identical markdown yields identical anchors.

Batch policy tests with synthetic watcher-event streams: a minimum quiet gap closes a batch; a continuous ~150 ms event stream is force-cut into discrete batches within the bounded window; an atomic rename-write yields exactly one batch; the hash-skip (disk content equals tab content) records nothing.

Snapshot-ring migration: the four recordSnapshot sites, the two recordOpenedSnapshot sites and the clearSnapshots site keep their call shape; the diff view opens and renders both the newest ring state and the replaceable opened baseline as before; all existing diff-view, opened-snapshot and live-reload specs stay green; an open followed by an external write produces exactly two records — a ring checkpoint of the pre-write buffer and an opened landing — and latestSnapshot still returns the pre-write buffer; after more than 50 in-app pauses snapshotCount stays 5, latestSnapshot still returns the last pre-reload state, openedSnapshot the last disk load; closing a tab through either close path leaves no journal entry.

Performance gate: the 10k-line fixture records a batch and computes its two-level diff within the plan-time budget on the test runner; the live-reload scroll-clamp e2e stays green and the V-M-025 open-file-timing budget is unchanged.
No UI and no backend: grep-pinned absence of new Vue components or Tauri commands introduced by this change; the library is importable and testable headlessly (vitest).

Attribution shape: actor model carries label/confidence fields but no production path sets them; a unit test pins that every ChangeRecord carries actor = {kind} with one of the three values, and a source assertion pins that no production path writes label or confidence.

npm test green; grace lint --path . --assertions current = 0; .grace/graph (new library module entry plus updated diffSnapshots/editor edges) and .grace/verification (journal, diff, batch-policy suites) updated in the same bundle.

src/renderer/src/store/editor.js — the four recordSnapshot sites and the two recordOpenedSnapshot sites keep their shape; consumption wiring only; CHANGE_SUMMARY updated.

NEW renderer library module (candidate location src/renderer/src/documentHistory/ — final location at plan time): journal, two-level diff, batch policy, actor model; MODULE_CONTRACT with ROLE: RUNTIME (the word "library" belongs in PURPOSE; the protocol role enum is RUNTIME | TEST | BARREL | CONFIG | TYPES | SCRIPT).
tests/renderer/ — new unit suites for journal, diff fixtures, batch policy, migration; performance fixture.
.grace/graph/ + .grace/verification/ — module and suite entries in the same bundle.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedCommand: npm test && npm run build && npx playwright test 'tests/e2e/diff-*.spec.ts' tests/e2e/live-reload-scroll.spec.ts --project=chromium
VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Unit suites green for journal records, two-level diff fixtures (EN+RU), batch-policy event streams and the snapshot-ring migration; existing diff-view and live-reload specs unchanged and green; performance fixture within the plan-time budget; grace lint --assertions current = 0 with graph/verification deltas in the bundle. Pre-implementation active-baseline check: run grace lint on main before starting; this evidence is the change's own gate, not a final-state claim.

Assumptions.Assumption: The dirty+liveReload silent-swap reading of APPLY_FILE_CHANGE (editor.js 2416-2573; gate 2458/2463, conflict branch 2516) is accurate: the reload branch runs for a dirty tab whenever liveReload is ON, with recordSnapshot preserving the pre-swap buffer. The repair fork is recorded as decided on 2026-10-23 — the repair ships as its own small fix bundle — and this bundle does not reopen it.
diff-match-patch is sufficient for fine-grained markdown diffs at document sizes Mark handles (tens of thousands of lines worst case); the performance gate exists to falsify this cheaply if wrong.

Content-derived anchors are computable from markdown alone: the headless block lexer src/muya/lib/parser/marked/lexer.js, with its shipped options pinned, produces the block token stream and no anchor depends on the transient ag-N ids or on rendered DOM. The anchoring rules are normative in R-2, not deferred to the plan.
Session-scoped memory is acceptable for every v1 consumer (agent-visibility v2 "since last viewed" works within a session; recovery-across-relaunch is explicitly v3).
